Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג - אי אמרת בשלמא, ר' יוחנן הכי קאמר: לאחר גמר דין מחלוקת, אבל לפני גמר דין — אפילו לרבנן חוזר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:1.english: This is the text we read: Granted, [if] Rabbi Yoḥanan says as follows: After the verdict [is issued] there is a dispute, but before the verdict [is issued] — even according to the Rabbis, [one can] retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:2.hebrew: רבא - דפסיק הלכתא דחוזר לפני גמר דין ולא לאחר גמר דין — דאמר כר' יוחנן ואליבא דרבנן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:2.english: Rava - Who ruled the halakha that [one can] retract before the verdict and not after the verdict — stated [his ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan and according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:3.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת - לר' יוחנן, בין בזה ובין בזה מחלוקת:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:3.english: But if you say - According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, the dispute is both in this [case] and in that [case].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:4.hebrew: רבא דאמר כמאן - בין לריש לקיש בין לר' יוחנן, לרבנן לפני גמר דין קאמרי דלא הדר. והא ליכא למימר דרבא כריש לקיש ואליבא דר"מ אמרה לשמעתיה — דלא שביק רבנן ועביד כר"מ, דפסקינן לקמן הלכה כחכמים. ולא שייך למימר הכא: רבא טעמא דנפשיה קאמר, וסבירא ליה דכי פליגי רבנן לאחר גמר דין, אבל לפני גמר דין מודו, אבל לרבי יוחנן בין בזו ובין בזו מחלוקת — דהא לא איירי רבא בפלוגתא כלל, אלא מיפסק פסק דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:10:4.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] is Rava stating [the halakha]? - Whether according to Reish Lakish or according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, according to the Rabbis, they say that before the verdict [one] cannot retract. And behold, it cannot be said that Rava stated his teaching in accordance with Reish Lakish and following [the view of] Rabbi Meir, for [Rava] would not abandon the Rabbis and act in accordance with Rabbi Meir, since we rule below [that] the halakha is in accordance with the Sages. Nor is it applicable to say here [that] Rava was stating his own reasoning, and he maintains that when the Rabbis disagree, [it is] after the verdict, but before the verdict they concede [that one can retract], whereas according to Rabbi Yoḥanan the dispute is both in this [case] and in that [case] — for Rava was not dealing with the dispute at all; rather, he was [simply] issuing a practical ruling.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:14:1.english: And they performed an act of acquisition with him - At the outset, so that he would not retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:15:1.english: And these are the ones who are disqualified - To judge and to testify.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:15:2.hebrew: המשחק בקוביא - כולהו מפרש בגמ', וכולן מעין גזלנין הן, והתורה אמרה (שמות כג): "אל תשת רשע עד" — וכל שכן דיין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:15:2.english: One who plays with dice - All of them are explained in the Gemara. And all of them are a type of robber, and the Torah said (Exodus 23): "Do not place a wicked person as a witness" — and all the more so a judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:15:3.hebrew: וסוחרי שביעית - הואיל וחימוד ממון מעבירו על דברי תורה, הוה ליה כרשע דחמס, ופסול לדון ולהעיד, שנוטה אחרי הבצע:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:15:3.english: And merchants of the Sabbatical [Year] - Since the coveting of money causes him to transgress the words of the Torah, he is considered like a wicked person of dishonest gain [rasha dechamas], and is disqualified from judging and from testifying, as he turns after unjust gain.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:16:1.hebrew: בתחילה היו קוראין אותן כו' - מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:16:1.english: Initially, they would call them, etc. - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:17:1.hebrew: שאין לו אומנות אלא הוא - דהואיל ואין עסוקין ביישובו של עולם, אינן בקיאין בטיב דינין ומשא ומתן, ואינן יראי חטא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:17:1.english: That he has no occupation other than this one - For since they are not engaged in the settlement of the world, they are not knowledgeable in the nature of laws and commerce, and they do not fear sin:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:18:1.hebrew: אסמכתא - היינו דבר דאינו נותן לו מדעתו, אלא סומך על דבר שאינו — דסבור שהוא יכול לנצח, ופעמים שמנצחין אותו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:18:1.english: An asmakhta - That is, a matter where he does not give [it] to him willingly, but rather relies on something that is not [certain] — as he assumes that he can win, and sometimes they defeat him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:18:2.english: Does not effect acquisition - And it is akin to stolen property in his possession.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:19:1.hebrew: כל כי האי גוונא לאו אסמכתא היא - והיכי דמי אסמכתא? כגון: דאם אוביר ולא אעביד, אשלם במיטבא (ב"מ דף עג:), וכגון משליש את שטרו דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח.) — דסומך על לא דבר, דסבור: "כל זה בידי לעשות", ומרישא, כי מתני, אדעתא דלא יהיב ליה לאסמכתא קא מתני, דטועה וסבור: "לא יבא לידי כך". אבל הכא, לא סמיך אמידי, דהא לא ידע אי נצח אי לא נצח, ואפי' הכי אתני. שמע מינה: מספיקא אתני, גמר ואקני, ולא גזילה היא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:19:1.english: Any case like this is not an asmakhta - And what is an example of an asmakhta? Such as: "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay from the best [produce]" (Bava Metzia 73b); and such as one who deposits his document with a third party [in the chapter] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a) — where he relies on an unfounded assumption, since he thinks: "All this is in my power to do"; and from the outset, when he stipulates, he stipulates with the intention not to give [it] to him, [stipulating merely] as an asmakhta, since he is mistaken and thinks: "It will not come to this." But here, he does not rely on anything, for he does not know whether he will win or not win; and even so, he stipulated. Conclude from this: he stipulated [despite the] uncertainty; he wholeheartedly resolved and transferred [ownership], and it is not robbery.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:1:1.hebrew: באותן הנשבעין - לפטור עצמן שלא ישלמו, דתובע קאמר: דור לי, ואני מוחל לך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:1:1.english: To those who take an oath - To exempt themselves so that they do not pay, for the claimant says: "Vow to me, and I will forgive you."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:2:1.hebrew: הנשבעין ונוטלין - השכיר והנגזל וכיוצא בהן, דנתבע קאמר ליה: "דור לי ואתן לך":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:2:1.english: Those who take an oath and collect - [Such as] the hired worker, the victim of robbery, and the like, where the defendant says to him: "Vow to me, and I will give [it to] you."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:3:1.hebrew: והא תנא לה רישא - דאוקמת לה באתן לך, ותרתי למה לי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:3:1.english: But behold, [the tanna] taught it in the first clause - For you established it [as a case of] "I will give you," and why do I need two [cases]?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:4:1.english: Makes [it] dependent on the decision of others - [Namely, the cases of] "my father" and "your father".

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:4:2.english: On his own decision - Of his fellow litigant.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:5:1.hebrew: מי יימר דמזכי ליה - ואי הוה ידע דמזכי ליה, לא הוה אמר. הלכך, הדר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:5:1.english: Who will say that [the judge] will rule in his favor - And had he known that [the judge] would rule in his [opponent's] favor, he would not have said [so]; therefore, he [can] retract.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:5:2.hebrew: אבל תולה בדעת עצמו - של בעל דין, אסיק אדעתיה דודאי נדר ליה כדי להפטר, וידע ומחיל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:5:2.english: But [where] he makes it dependent on his own decision - [Meaning, the decision] of the litigant [himself]: He took into account that [the debtor] would certainly vow to him in order to be exempt, and [yet] he knew [this] and forgave [the debt].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:7:1.hebrew: לפני גמר דין - לאחר שטענו בפניהם, וקודם גמר דין בא זה לחזור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 24b:7:1.english: Before the verdict - After they presented their claims before them, and prior to the verdict, this [litigant] came to retract.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:10:1.hebrew: רבא דאמר כמאן - וליכא למימר דסבירא ליה כר"ש בן לקיש אליבא דר' מאיר. חדא, כפירוש רש"י: דאין לומר דשביק רבנן ועביד כר' מאיר; ועוד, דהכא פליגי ר' יוחנן ור"ש בן לקיש, ורבא פסיק פרק החולץ (יבמות דף לו.) כר"ש בן לקיש בתלת, משמע דבכל שאר מקומות ס"ל כר' יוחנן לגבי רשב"ל. וליכא למימר: הכא טעמיה דנפשיה קאמר, כדתירץ לעיל — משום דהכא לא קאי אפלוגתא דמתני' כדלעיל, דמשום הכי מפרש לה לעיל טעמיה דנפשיה, אבל הכא ליכא למימר טעמיה דנפשיה קאמר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:10:1.english: "In accordance with whose [opinion] is Rava stating [the halakha]?" - And one cannot say that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish according to Rabbi Meir. First, as Rashi explained: for one cannot say that he would leave [aside the opinion of] the Rabbis and act in accordance with Rabbi Meir. And furthermore, here Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish disagree, and Rava ruled in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36a) in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish in [only] three [cases], which implies that in all other places he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan against Rashbal. And one cannot say: "Here [too] he is stating his own reasoning," as [the Gemara] answered above — because here he is not addressing the dispute of the Mishnah, as [he was] above, which is why above [the Gemara] explained [that he is stating] his own reasoning; but here, one cannot say that he is stating his own reasoning.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:12:1.hebrew: שלח ליה לאחר גמר דין מחלוקת והלכה כדברי חכמים - תימה: דהכא משמע דלאחר גמר דין מחלוקת, אבל קודם — יכול לחזור בו. ובפ' יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכח. ושם) אמרי': אמר לו "עבדי גנבת", "שורי טבחת", והלה אומר "אתה מכרתו לי", "אתה נתתו לי במתנה, רצונך השבע וטול" — נשבע ואינו יכול לחזור בו; משמע: מיד שאמר "השבע וטול" שחבירו ישבע — ואינו יכול לחזור בו, אלמא אפי' קודם גמר דין אינו יכול לחזור בו! להכי גרס ר"ת: "ונשבע — אינו יכול לחזור בו", כלומר: אם קפץ זה חבירו ונשבע — אינו יכול לחזור בו, דכיון דכבר נשבע — הוי לאחר גמר דין, ואמרי' לאחר גמר דין דהלכה כחכמים:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:12:1.english: He sent to him: The dispute is after the verdict, and the halakha is in accordance with the statement of the Rabbis - [This is] difficult, for here it implies that the dispute is after the verdict, but prior [to it], he can retract; yet in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Noḥalin (Bava Batra 128a, and there) we say: [If] one said to him, "You stole my slave," [or] "You slaughtered my ox," and the other says, "You sold it to me," [or] "You gave it to me as a gift; if you wish, swear and take [it]" — he swears and cannot retract. This implies [that] immediately once he said "Swear and take," his fellow may swear and he cannot retract, which proves that even before the verdict he cannot retract! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam had the reading: "Ve-nishba [And he swore] — he cannot retract," that is to say: If this one, his fellow, jumped ahead and swore, he cannot retract, because once he has already sworn, it is [considered] after the verdict, and we say [that] after the verdict the halakha is in accordance with the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:15:1.hebrew: ואלו הן הפסולין - יש גורסין עבדים, משום דסבירא ליה דקא חשיב הכא פסולי דרבנן ודאורייתא. ולא נהירא, משום דלא חשיב במתני' רק פסולי דרבנן, דהא גזלנים לא קתני, וכל פסולי דמתני' פסולי דרבנן נינהו: משחק בקוביא — אפי' למ"ד אסמכתא היא, דאסמכתא לא קניא, מ"מ אינו דאורייתא, כיון שאינו סבור לעשות איסור לבא לידי פסול דאורייתא; ולמ"ד משום ישובו של עולם, פשיטא דאינו אלא מדרבנן. ומלוה בריבית — מיירי בריבית שאינה קצוצה; ואפי' מיירי בריבית שקצוצה, לא משמע ליה איסור, כיון דמדעתיה יהיב, ואינו פסול לעדות אלא מדרבנן. מפריחי יונים — מדרבנן פסולים: אפי' למ"ד "אי תקדמי יונך", היינו משחק בקוביא; ולאידך דאמר "ארא", מפני דרכי שלום הוא. וסוחרי שביעית — מיירי בשביעית בזמן הזה, דאינו אסור אלא מדרבנן; ואפי' בשביעית דאורייתא, לא חשיב ליה איסור, הא דממציאין מעות לעניים. אבל עבדים — פסולין מדאורייתא נינהו, ק"ו מאשה: ומה אשה שכשירה לבא בקהל פסולה להעיד, דכתיב (דברים יט) "האנשים", עבד שפסול וכו'. על כן נראה דלא גרסי' עבדים, דלא מיירי אלא בפסולי דרבנן:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:15:1.english: And these are the ones who are disqualified - Some read "slaves" [in the text of the Mishnah], because they maintain that [the Mishnah] here enumerates [both] rabbinically and biblically disqualified [witnesses]. But this is not plausible, because [the Tanna] enumerates in the Mishnah only rabbinically disqualified [individuals], for behold, he does not teach "robbers" [who are disqualified by Torah law], and all of the disqualified individuals in the Mishnah are rabbinically disqualified: One who plays with dice — even according to the one who said [that he is disqualified because] it is an asmachta [a conditional wager], and an asmachta does not effect legal acquisition [and so taking the money is considered robbery], nevertheless it is not [a] biblical [disqualification], since he does not consider that he is committing a prohibition so as to incur a biblical disqualification; and according to the one who said [that he is disqualified] because [he does not engage in] the settlement of the world, it is obvious that it is only rabbinic. And one who lends with interest — [the Mishnah] is dealing with interest that is not fixed [by Torah law, i.e., rabbinic interest]; and even if it is dealing with fixed interest [prohibited by the Torah], it does not seem like a prohibition to him, since [the borrower] gives it of his own volition, and [thus] he is disqualified from testimony only rabbinically. Those who fly pigeons — are rabbinically disqualified: even according to the one who said [it refers to wagering:] "If your pigeon precedes [mine]," that is [equivalent to] one who plays with dice; and according to the other [opinion] who said [it refers to baiting pigeons with] an ara [a decoy/call], it is [only prohibited] on account of the ways of peace. And merchants of the Sabbatical Year — [the Mishnah] is dealing with the Sabbatical Year in this era, which is prohibited only rabbinically; and even during a biblically [mandated] Sabbatical Year, he does not consider this [practice] of providing money to the poor [to gather produce on their behalf] a prohibition. However, slaves are disqualified by biblical law, through an a fortiori [kal vaḥomer] deduction from a woman: If a woman, who is eligible to enter the congregation [in marriage], is disqualified from testifying, as it is written: "the men" (Deuteronomy 19:17), a slave, who is disqualified [from entering the congregation, is it not all the more so that he is disqualified from testifying]! Therefore, it appears that we should not read "slaves," for [the Mishnah] deals only with rabbinically disqualified [individuals].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:19:1.hebrew: כל כי האי גוונא לאו אסמכתא היא - פ"ה דהיכי דמי אסמכתא? כגון: "אם אוביר ולא אעביד אשלם במיטבא", וכן משליש את שטרו דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח. ושם), דכל הני סמיך אדעתיה וסבור הוא שזה בידו לעשות, ומרישא כי מתני ליה — אדעתיה דלא יהיב ליה מתנה אתני ליה, שהרי סבור הוא שלא יבא לידי כך. אבל הכא, לאו בידו, ולא סמיך אמידי, דהא לא ידע אי נצח אי לא נצח, ואפ"ה אתני; ש"מ דמספיקא גמר ומקני, ולאו גזילה היא. ומיהו הא (שפיר) דאם אוביר ולא אעביד אשלם במיטבא אסמכתא היא — טעות סופרים הוא זה, ובזה לא דבר רש"י; דהא אם אוביר אשלם במיטבא לאו אסמכתא, כדאמרי' פ' איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף עד.), אלא היינו: "אם אוביר ולא אעביד אשלם אלפא זוזי", דבפ' המקבל (בבא מציעא דף קד.) קאמר אסמכתא היא. ובפי' רש"י היה כתוב "אם אוביר וכו'", על כן טעו סופרים. אבל ר"ת הקשה לפי' הקונט', משום דלפי פי' משמע דטפי חשיב אסמכתא (מה) שהיה בידו מלאו בידו. ובפ' איזהו נשך (בבא מציעא דף עד. ושם) משמע איפכא, דאמר התם: "האי מאן דמקבל זוזי מחבריה למזבין ליה חמרא ופשע ולא זבין משלם כדאזיל אפרוותא דזולשפוט", וקאמר התם דאסמכתא היא כו', עד דמקשה הש"ס: מאי שנא מאם אוביר ולא אעביד אשלם במיטבא? ומשני: התם גבי אם אוביר ולא אעביד אשלם במיטבא, משום דהוי בידו לא הויא אסמכתא — אלמא דלא הויא בידו הוי טפי אסמכתא ממה שהוא בידו! על כן נראה לר"ת לפרש הכי: "כל כי האי גוונא לאו אסמכתא היא", דלא הויא אסמכתא אלא היכא שאין יכול להרויח, כגון משליש שטרו וכו' דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח.); אבל הכא לא הויא אסמכתא, משום דכיון דשנים הם, כל אחד ואחד מקני לחבריה, מגו דאי מרווח בעי איהו למקני — בההיא הנאה גמר ומקני לחבריה. ולפי זה, כל שידוכין לא הויא אסמכתא, משום דכל חד וחד בעי למקני — גמר נמי ומקני. ומיהו קשה על פי' ר"ת, שהרי בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מח: ושם) אמרינן: "הנותן עירבון לחבירו ואמר לו: אם אני חוזר בי עירבוני מחול לך, והלה אומר: אם אני חוזר בי אכפול לך ערבונך — נתקיימו התנאים, דברי רבי יוסי"; ומסיק התם לבסוף אליבא דר' יהודה דהויא אסמכתא ולא קניא — אלמא אפי' בשנים חשיב אסמכתא, ולא אמרינן מגו דאי בעי קנין העירבון אם חבירו חוזר בו מקנה נמי כנגד העירבון לחבירו כשהוא חוזר בו! ועוד משמע לקמן גבי צריכותות דמפריחי יונים, דהיכא שהוא סבור דבידו להרויח הויא אסמכתא בעלמא טפי, כדפירש רש"י. על כן נראה לר"י עיקר כפירוש רש"י. ואי קשיא לו מההיא דאיזהו נשך כדפירש לעיל, תריץ הכי: שאני התם, דודאי דבר שהוא בידו ממש לגמרי, כגון "אם אוביר ולא איעביד אשלם במיטבא" — דהתם בידו לעשות, ולא גזים נמי, שסובר הוא שכך הפסיד חבירו אם לא ישלים תנאו, כמו אם ישלם במיטבא; ובההיא ודאי גמר ומקני ולא חשיב אסמכתא, ואומר בלבו: "עלי לשלם ודאי מן הדין מה שבידי לעשות ולא עשיתי". אבל היכא דגזים, אע"ג דהוי בידו ממש לגמרי, כגון "אם אוביר ולא איעבד אשלם אלפא זוזי" — מכל מקום כיון דגזים, ודאי הוי גוזמא דמתנה לשלם אלף זוז בשביל קרקע אחת, ודאי חשיב אסמכתא. ומיהו קשה, דהכא משמע דדבר דלא הוי בידו לאו אסמכתא הוא, כגון משחק בקוביא דהכא, ואע"ג דגזים; ומאי שנא מההיא דחמרא דזולשפוט דחשבינן אסמכתא מהאי טעמא? ומכ"מ לא קשיא מידי: דהתם ודאי הויא אסמכתא משום שזה סומך עליו, משום דהוי דבר שבידו שמוצאין יין למכור, ונראה כאסמכתא קצת אע"ג דלא גזים, דשמא לא ירצו אחרים למכור לו; והלכך, אע"ג דלא גזים, כיון דלאו בידו הוא לגמרי, לא גמר ומקני לחבריה. אבל הכא גבי משחק בקוביא, דלאו בידו הוא כלל, אע"ג דגזים בתנאי שחוק שלו, מ"מ גמר ומקני; דכיון שהוא יודע שאין בידו להרויח, וידוע הוא שאחד מהם ירויח, ודאי לא נתכוון להסמיך חבירו על דבר שאינו, אלא גמר ומקנה — לכך כי האי גוונא ודאי לאו אסמכתא היא. אבל הא דאשלם אלפא זוזי, דגזים וגם בידו להשלים תנאו, יש לנו לומר דנתכוון להסמיך ולהטעות חבירו, הויא אסמכתא משום דגוזמא קאמר ולא גמר ומקנה; ומסתברא דלהכי גזים שהוא סבור ודאי שיעבדנה, ועוד שבידו הוא. ומשום הכי פסק דמשחק בקוביא כשר לעדות, דפסקינן כר' יהודה לקמן דכיון שיש לו אומנות שלא הוא כשר. והא דפסקינן דמשחק בקוביא קני — דווקא כשמעות שניהם על פי הדף, לפי שהדף והמקום קנוי לאותו שירויח כדי לקנות המעות אשר עליו; אבל המשחקים באמנה, אפילו הקנו לא מהני אם לא הקנו בב"ד חשוב, כדאי' בנדרים (דף כז:):
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 24b:19:1.english: "Any case like this is not an asmakhta" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: What is an example of an asmakhta? For example: "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay with the best [produce]"; and likewise, one who deposits his promissory note [with a third party] in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a and there). For in all these cases, he relies on his own mindset and thinks that this is in his power to do; and from the beginning, when he makes the stipulation with him, he stipulates on the assumption that he will not [have to] give him a gift, for he believes that it will not come to this. But here [in dice playing], it is not in his power, and he does not rely on anything, for he does not know whether he will win or not win, and even so he made the stipulation! Conclude from this that out of the uncertainty, he wholeheartedly resolves to transfer [ownership], and it is not robbery. However, this [text which states] that "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay with the best [produce]" is an asmakhta is a scribal error, and Rashi did not say this! For "if I let [it] lie fallow, I will pay with the best" is not an asmakhta, as we say in the chapter Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 74a). Rather, this [intended example] is: "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay one thousand zuz," concerning which [the Gemara] in the chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 104a) states that it is an asmakhta. And in Rashi's commentary it was written: "If I let [it] lie fallow, etc.", and therefore scribes erred. However, Rabbeinu Tam challenged the explanation of the Kuntres, because according to [Rashi's] explanation, it implies that something that was in his power [to perform] is considered more of an asmakhta than [something] not in his power; yet in the chapter Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 74a and there), the opposite is implied! For [the Gemara] states there: "One who receives money from another to buy wine for him, and was negligent and did not buy [it], pays according to [the cheap price at which wine] goes in the port of Zulshafat." And [the Gemara] states there that this is an asmakhta, etc., until the Shas asks: How is this different from "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay with the best [produce]"? And [the Gemara] answers: There, regarding "if I let [it] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay with the best," because it is in his power, it is not an asmakhta. This proves that something that is not in his power is more of an asmakhta than what is in his power! Therefore, it seems [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam to explain as follows: "Any case like this is not an asmakhta" — for it is not an asmakhta except where he cannot gain, such as one who deposits his promissory note, etc., in Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a). But here, it is not an asmakhta, because since they are two [parties], each one transfers [ownership] to the other: since if he gains, he wants to acquire, in exchange for that benefit he wholeheartedly resolves to transfer to his fellow. And according to this, any matchmaking agreement (shidukhin) is not an asmakhta, because since each one wants to acquire [the penalty if the other breaches], he also wholeheartedly resolves to transfer. However, there is a difficulty against Rabbeinu Tam's explanation: For behold, in the chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 48b and there), we say: "One who gives a deposit to another and said to him: 'If I renege, my deposit is forgiven to you,' and the other says: 'If I renege, I will double your deposit for you' — the conditions are fulfilled, [these are] the words of Rabbi Yosei." And [the Gemara] concludes there in the end, according to Rabbi Yehudah, that it is an asmakhta and he does not acquire [it]. This proves that even with two [parties making reciprocal stipulations], it is considered an asmakhta, and we do not say that since he wants acquisition of the deposit if his fellow reneges, he also transfers [the sum] corresponding to the deposit to his fellow when he reneges! Furthermore, it is implied later on regarding the mutual necessities of "those who fly pigeons" that where one thinks it is in his power to gain, it is generally more of an asmakhta, as Rashi explained. Therefore, it seems to the Ri that the primary [view] is like Rashi's explanation. And if it is difficult to him from that [passage] in Eizehu Neshekh as explained above, resolve it as follows: There it is different, for certainly a matter that is truly and completely in his power, such as "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay with the best [produce]" — where it is in his power to do, and he also did not exaggerate (lo gazim), for he reasons that his fellow lost this much if he does not fulfill his condition, just as if he pays with the best [produce]; and in that case he certainly wholeheartedly resolves to transfer and it is not considered an asmakhta, and he says in his heart: "It is certainly incumbent upon me by law to pay for what was in my power to do and I did not do." But where he exaggerates (gazim), even though it is truly and completely in his power, such as "If I let [the field] lie fallow and do not cultivate [it], I will pay one thousand zuz," nevertheless, since he exaggerated, it is certainly an exaggeration (guzma), for he stipulates to pay one thousand zuz on account of a single piece of land; it is certainly considered an asmakhta. However, [another] difficulty arises: for here it implies that something that is not in his power is not an asmakhta, such as one who plays dice here, and even though he exaggerates; so how is this different from that [case] of the wine of Zulshafat, which we consider an asmakhta for this reason? And nevertheless, it is not difficult at all: For there, it is certainly an asmakhta because this [buyer] relies on him, since it is a matter in his power inasmuch as wine is found for sale, and it appears somewhat like an asmakhta even though he did not exaggerate, lest others might not want to sell to him; and therefore, even though he did not exaggerate, since it is not completely in his power, he does not wholeheartedly resolve to transfer to his fellow. But here regarding one who plays dice, where it is not in his power at all, even though he exaggerates in the conditions of his game, nevertheless he wholeheartedly resolves to transfer; for since he knows that it is not in his power to win, and it is known that one of them will win, he certainly did not intend to cause his fellow to rely on something that does not exist, but rather he wholeheartedly resolves to transfer. Therefore, any case like this is certainly not an asmakhta. However, that [case] of "I will pay one thousand zuz," where he exaggerated and it was also in his power to fulfill his condition, we must say that he intended to cause [his fellow] to rely and to mislead his fellow; it is an asmakhta because he spoke exaggeratedly (guzma) and did not wholeheartedly resolve to transfer. And it stands to reason that the reason he exaggerated is that he thought he would certainly cultivate it, and furthermore, that it is in his power. And for this reason, [the Gemara] ruled that a dice player is qualified for testimony, for we rule in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah later on that since he has another occupation besides it, he is qualified. And that which we rule that a dice player acquires [his winnings] is specifically when the money of both of them is on the board, because the board and the space are acquired by the one who will win in order to acquire the money that is on it; but those who play on credit (be'amanah), even if they performed a formal act of acquisition, it is not effective unless they performed the acquisition in a prominent court of law, as stated in Nedarim (27b).
